headline: Protein language model embeddings and structured decoders advance sequence annotation tasks
label: Deep Learning Sequence Annotation
summary: Neural sequence models with structured decoding are now applied to gene, protein domain and repeat annotation, often with protein language model embeddings.
synthesis: The three items share a common architecture: a neural model produces per-base or per-residue predictions, and a decoding step converts these into consistent annotations. deeprok pairs a base-level network with overlap-aware decoding and a neural start-site ranker, reducing prokaryotic gene prediction errors. PSALM takes ESM-2 protein language model embeddings through a per-residue classifier and a structured decoder to produce non-overlapping protein domain annotations. TREAD applies supervised residue-level labelling to protein language model embeddings for repeat annotation and reports outperforming HMMER on RepeatsDB and Pfam benchmarks. The new element relative to profile-based methods such as HMMER is the use of learned embeddings in place of hand-built profiles, combined with decoders that enforce annotation consistency. The evidence presented is benchmark-based comparison.
